bge_reranker.node_purpose: Score every candidate against every bounded RetrievalNeed so the BGE cross-encoder, rather than a different embedding route, chooses the question that the candidate can answer.
bge_reranker.input_scale: At most 96 candidates per atom across 66 total bounded needs: no more than 6,336 query-candidate pairs for the eighteen-atom development set.
required_outputs: one finite score per candidate-need pair
bge_reranker.schema_burden: flat pair scores followed by deterministic candidate-major aggregation
bge_reranker.materiality_and_quality_risk: preselecting one need with BGE multi-vector made both cross-encoders answer a potentially wrong question; scoring all finite needs removes that cross-model selector bias
bge_reranker.comparable_run_evidence: v1.2 candidate generation recalled 13/15 positive atoms but BGE and Qwen rerankers placed only 0/15 and 1/15 in the top ten when both inherited one BGE-selected need
bge_reranker.reasoning_profile: local cross-encoder scoring; no generation, network access or training
bge_reranker.stop_and_truncation: maximum 1024 tokens per pair, batch 2, exact 6,336-or-fewer pair count, fail on any score-count or candidate/need identity drift

qwen_reranker.node_purpose: Independently score every candidate against every bounded RetrievalNeed and select Qwen's own best-matching need before ranking.
qwen_reranker.input_scale: At most 96 candidates per atom across 66 total bounded needs: no more than 6,336 query-candidate pairs for the eighteen-atom development set.
required_outputs: one finite score per candidate-need pair
qwen_reranker.schema_burden: flat pair scores followed by deterministic candidate-major aggregation
qwen_reranker.materiality_and_quality_risk: a Qwen reranker result is not meaningful when BGE chose its query; independent all-need scoring tests actual direct-answerability without granting Evidence authority
qwen_reranker.comparable_run_evidence: v1.2 Qwen placed 1/15 registered positive atoms in the top ten while VS1 pricing-and-mix reached the top five, indicating query-selection instability rather than a universal model failure
qwen_reranker.reasoning_profile: local instruction-aware cross-encoder scoring; no generation, network access or training
qwen_reranker.stop_and_truncation: maximum 1024 tokens per pair, batch 2, exact 6,336-or-fewer pair count, fail on any score-count or candidate/need identity drift

why_new_attempt_is_justified: The v1.2 candidate pool recalled thirteen of fifteen positive atoms, so the dominant remaining error is after candidate generation.

Both cross-encoders were forced to score each candidate against one RetrievalNeed selected by BGE multi-vector, which creates cross-model selector bias and can make a strong reranker answer the wrong question.
The RetrievalNeed set is finite, immutable and already compiled before labels, so scoring every candidate-need pair does not leak qrels or broaden the request.
Object-level CandidateDecision has proved that source review alone cannot repair a poor candidate head.
